pageCache.text:
Prospective Parents
Prospective Parent Tours
Please contact the school office to arrange a tour of our fantastic school.
Tours are typically run on a Monday morning at 9am - these must be booked in advance.
Please ring 01403 790253 or email the office.
Dear Prospective Parents and Carers,
Thank you for expressing an interest in sending your child to Slinfold CE Primary School. I hope that visiting our website and viewing our school video, which can be found on the 'Welcome' page, helps you to gain a good understanding of our caring and nurturing school community.
Slinfold has 5 classes to cover the 7 year groups and if your child joins us in Reception then they will join Hamble Class. This is a mixed Reception and Year One class that has the potential to include 20 children from Reception and 10 from Year One.
Hamble Class work closely with Medway Class which is our mixed Year One and Year Two class. They follow the same topics, mix together for certain learning sessions, and their building has the feel of a lovely and small infant school.
Hamble Class are fortunate that they have a beautiful covered outdoor space in which to learn as well as direct access to the playground. This outdoor learning space is linked to our Pre-School and the children in Hamble love seeing the younger children while they are learning.

pageCache.text:
SEND Resources
SENDIAS
West Sussex SENDIAS (SEND Information, Advice and Support) Service provides information, advice and support to children and young people who have special educational needs and/or disabilities and to their parent carers. There service is free, impartial and confidential.
Intervention
Please click on the name of the intervention your child is receiving to find out more.
The impact of these will be tracked via your child's ILP which will be reviewed on a termly basis.
Sometimes there are bespoke interventions created specifically to meet the needs of your child. Please speak to your child's class teacher or Mrs Collins for more information on these.
Sensory Circuits
Individual Reading
Social Skills Groups
Phonics Booster
Play Therapy
Narrative Therapy
Lego Therapy
Working Memory
Zones of regulation
The Zones of Regulation is the original framework and curriculum (Kuypers, 2011) that develops awareness of feelings, energy and alertness levels while exploring a variety of tools and strategies for regulation, prosocial skills, self-care, and overall wellness. This curriculum provides us an easy way to think and talk about how we feel on the inside and sort these feelings into four colored Zones, all of which are expected in life. Once we understand our feelings and zones, we can learn to use tools/strategies to manage our different Zones in order to meet goals like doing schoolwork or other tasks, managing big feelings, and healthy relationships with others. The simple, common language and visual structure of The Zones of Regulation helps make the complex skill of regulation more concrete for learners and those who support them.
Dyslexia Friendly Books
Does your child struggle to read due to dyslexia or visual stress? Are they reluctant to engage with books or read for pleasure? We work with the best writers and illustrators to publish super-readable, accessible books that help every child experience the joy of reading.
More information can be found on the following link.
Barrington Books
Social Stories
Social Stories are short descriptions of a particular situation, event or activity, which include specific information about what to expect in that situation and why.
Social stories can be used to:
develop self-care skills (for example, how to clean teeth, wash hands or get dressed), social skills (for example, sharing, asking for help, saying thank you, interrupting) and academic abilities
help someone to understand how others might behave or respond in a particular situation
help a person to cope with changes to routine and unexpected or distressing events (for example, absence of teacher, moving house, thunderstorms)
provide positive feedback to a person about an area of strength or achievement in order to develop self-esteem
as a behavioural strategy (for example, what to do when angry, how to cope with anxiety).

Attendance Matters
Our school attendance target this year is 95%!
We have gone up from 94.7% to 94.9%!
- Incredible effort everyone, we're almost there!
What if my child needs to miss school?
Parents and carers have a legal duty to ensure your child gets a full time-education.
There are only a small number of circumstances where missing a school day is permitted. Your child must attend every day that the school is open, unless:
These are the only circumstances where schools can permit your child to be absent.
Absence Notification Form.docx
Your child is too ill to attend.
What counts as an exceptional circumstance?
School leaders are responsible for deciding what counts as an exceptional circumstance when it comes to a child missing school.
They should look at each application individually, considering the specific facts and background context. If a leave of absence is granted, the school will decide how long the pupil can be away from school.
Holidays are very rarely an acceptable reason for a school absence and are unlikely to be treated as an exceptional circumstance.
Sickness
In the unfortunate event that your child becomes ill at home or school we will follow the guidance outlined by Public Health England.
If you child becomes unwell at school we will call to discuss suitable steps in order to support their well-being. If your child is ill at home please do contact the school office by 8:40 on 01403 790253 to notify us of their absence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Slinfold CE Primary School and Pre-School - Personal Development
pageCache.text:
Personal Development
At Slinfold CE Primary School, Personal Development is the thread that runs through the curriculum, and offers our children the strategies and skills they need to become active, responsible and respectful members of the wider community.
All of our children are known and celebrated as individuals and are challenged to be their very best through the core curriculum, wider curriculum and enrichment opportunities offered to all.
Through Personal Development we aim to:
Some of these areas of Personal Development are taught explicitly through our PSHE / Relationships & Sex Education, while others are linked to our daily worship, enrichment days, off-site visits and our values, which we hold at the centre of everything we do.
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development
Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural Development is essential for children's individual development, as well as the development of society as a whole.
Spiritual Development
Children’s spiritual development involves the growth of their sense of self, their unique potential, their understanding of their strengths and weaknesses, and their will to achieve. As their curiosity about themselves and their place in the world increases, they try to answer for themselves some of life’s fundamental questions. They develop the knowledge, skills, understanding, qualities and attitudes they need to foster their own inner lives and non-material wellbeing.
Moral development involves children acquiring an understanding of the difference between right and wrong and of moral conflict, a concern for others and the will to do what is right. They are able and willing to reflect on the consequences of their actions and learn how to forgive themselves and others. They develop the knowledge, skills and understanding, qualities and attitudes they need in order to make responsible moral decisions and act on them.
Social development involves children acquiring an understanding of the responsibilities and rights of being members of families and communities (local, national and global), and an ability to relate to others and to work with others for the common good. They display a sense of belonging and an increasing willingness to participate. They develop the knowledge, skills, understanding, qualities and attitudes they need to become active citizens within their community.
Cultural Development
Cultural development involves children acquiring an understanding of cultural traditions and heritage, and the ability to appreciate and respond to ‘the arts’. The children will acquire a respect for their own culture and that of others, an interest in others’ ways of doing things and curiosity about differences. They develop the knowledge, skills, understanding, qualities and attitudes they need to understand, appreciate and contribute to culture.
Personal Development

pageCache.pageTitle: Slinfold CE Primary School and Pre-School - Individual Reading
pageCache.text:
Individual Reading
Individual Reading involves your child reading to an adult on a 1:1 basis. Regular reading is important because it provides your child with an opportunity to practise decoding texts, applying their phonic knowledge and rehearsing the reading of whole words too. Most importantly, it is an opportunity to discuss the text, developing comprehension, vocabulary, imagination and concentration.
Intended Outcomes:
· For your child to increase in pace and fluency.
· For your child to recognise an increasing number of phonemes.
· For your child to recognise an increasing number of words.
· For your child to develop a better understanding of what they are reading.
· For your child to increasingly enjoy reading and want to read more at home.
What can you do to help at home?
Be a good reading role model.

Meet the Governors
Welcome from the Co-Chairs of Governors
As Co-Chairs of Governors, we would like to thank you for your interest in Slinfold Church of England Primary School and Pre-School. Our vibrant and successful school is set in the heart of this attractive West Sussex village and is the focal point for several community events including our annual Summer Fair, usually held in May. Our ethos is firmly grounded in Christianity and we enjoy strong links with St Peter's Church.
The school is lucky to benefit from extensive grounds, including a wonderful environmental area, where we run our Forest School programme for all pupils with a dedicated, trained practitioner.
We pride ourselves in treating all children as individuals and really strive to get the best from every pupil. We are small enough to know and value every child and encourage them to aim high in all areas of the curriculum, whether that be athletics, algebra or art! Everyone can excel at something and we endeavour to uncover the talents of every child and enable them to flourish.
We also have a thriving Pre-School on site which shares our facilities. This close physical relationship ensures excellent communication between staff, making the transition to Reception seamless and easy for the younger children.
We look forward to welcoming you and your family to our school so please come and visit us to find out more and meet our staff and children.
Sally Westwood and Davie Robertson, Co-Chairs of Governors
What is a Governing Body?
The Government requires that each school has a management team known as a governing body. This team is made up of the various stakeholders that the school serves (parents, local authority, staff, diocese and community). Governors are either elected or appointed, e.g. parent governors are elected from the parent body; the local authority appoints LA governors, the governing body appoints community governors and foundation governors are elected by the diocese.
What are the three core functions of a Governing body?
How is the Governing body structured?
At Slinfold CE Primary School, we meet as a Full Governing Body (FGB) on at least six occasions throughout the year. Like most schools, we operate without separate committees but as a full GB working collaboratively. In addition, where working parties are required to monitor particular areas of school life, these are formed as necessary. We do, however, operate a pay panel and a headteacher’s appraisal committee.
Clerk to Governors: Mrs Tanya Payne

I was a GP in Glasgow for a number of years and then spent the last 16 years at Ford open prison where I set up a GP practice within the prison (The new fence may make me feel more at home !) I’m a keen golfer, mindfulness teacher and I am enjoying the new-found freedom of retirement. I feel very privileged to be part of the Slinfold community and, as the school is one of the most important facets of this great community, I hope to contribute in a small way to it continuing to thrive and flourish."

SEND
Welcome to Slinfold CE Primary School SEND Support. I am Claire Collins, and I'm the Deputy Headteacher and Inclusion Leader. I hope you find this page helpful in explaining how children with SEND are supported in our school. There is also further information regarding outside organisations who can also help you support your children. If you have any questions regarding SEND, please contact me through the school office by telephone 01403 790253 or via email.
Special Education Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
At Slinfold CE Primary School, we acknowledge the individual needs of our children and employ strategies to meet these. The strategies may include using different resources or providing a child with additional group or individual support.
A child who receives additional support is monitored closely through a process of Assess-Plan-Do-Review which is in line with the requirements of the SEND Code of Practice (2014). The parents and carers of children receiving additional support are kept informed about their child's progress through both verbal and written feedback. The school acknowledges the importance of working closely with parents and carers, and their views are always sought.
Sometimes the school may also draw on the expertise of outside professionals like Speech and Language Therapists and Educational Psychologists.
We are committed to providing a full and inclusive curriculum for all of our children. All areas of the school are accessible and we have a purpose-built sensory room.
Further details on how the school and West Sussex support children with SEND can be found in the Local offer documents below.
West Sussex Local Offer
Every local authority has to display their offer of Special Needs Provision and services available for children with disabilities and Special Educational Needs. This is called the ‘Local Offer’. The intention is to offer choice, transparency and information for families, as well as providing a resource for professionals to detail the range of services and provision locally.

A group of our pupils proudly represented the school at the Horsham District Cross Country event held at Christ’s Hospital on Tuesday 24th March. All of the children ran with great enthusiasm, showing impressive resilience and determination throughout their races. We are incredibly proud of their positive attitudes, teamwork, and commitment on what was a fantastic day of sport.
On Wednesday 14th January, we took a team of 10 children to The Weald to take part in a Tag Rugby Tournament. The children showed amazing team work, supporting each other on the pitch and persevered when the games got tough! Well done team!
On 8th October, we took a group of children to The Weald School for a Multi Skills festival. The children took part in a wide range of sporting activities alongside other local schools.
We are incredibly proud of a group of our pupils who recently represented the school at a gymnastics competition held at The Weald School, on Monday 15th March.
Competing with determination and enthusiasm, the team achieved outstanding success.
Throughout the event, the children demonstrated not only their fantastic gymnastic skills, but also exemplary behaviour, teamwork, and resilience. They truly embodied our school values in every aspect of the competition, supporting one another and showing great sportsmanship.
Well done to all involved—we couldn’t be prouder of your achievements!
2024 - 2025 Sports Reports
On Monday 9th June, 6 of our Year 6 children attended a dance workshop at The Weald. The children showed great energy and enthusiasm for dance and demonstrated incredible teamwork skills. Great work team!
On Wednesday 14th May, we took a group of 7 children to The Weald for a Tri Golf festival. The children learnt how to swing the club for an accurate shot. All the children worked incredibly hard, supporting one another and encouraging those who were less confident. Well done team!
On Wednesday 7th May, we took all the Year 1 children to The Weald to take part in a Multi Skills event. The children really enjoyed the afternoon, they listened well to the instructions given for each activity and performed them with great enthusiasm. The tunnel activity was the children’s favourite, as they got to race one another.
On Monday 17th March, we took 7 year 4 and 5 girls to The Weald to take part in a locality Gymnastics competition. I was blown away by their enthusiasm towards this event. They all competed incredibly well, showing off their floor and vault skills. It was commented by the organisers that our team showed such great team work and really supported each other whilst completing their individual routines. Well done girls, another great success!
KS1 Multi Skills Festival
On Wednesday 22th November, we took a group of Year 1 children to The Weald secondary school to take part in a Multi Skills Festival with other local schools. The children enjoyed an array of different sporting activities throughout the afternoon, demonstrating their sporting skills in each.
On Wednesday 6th November, we took a group of children to compete in The Weald Cross Country event against other local primary schools. The children showed real determination, supporting each other as they ran. Arlo came 5th in the Year 3/4 boys race, Fynn came 6th in the Year 6 boys race and Kim came 10th in the Year 5 girls race! Well done to everyone for taking part in such a brilliant event!
On Tuesday 21st October, we sent a team of 7 girls to take part in a girl's basketball festival at Collyers Sixth Form College. The girls showed great sportsmanship, and worked amazingly well as a team.
2023 - 2024 Sports Reports
Our annual sports week took place during the week commencing 24th June 2024. During the week, the children had an opportunity to take part in different sporting workshops, including -
- Football with North Horsham Soccer Academy
- Cricket with Horsham School Sports
- Tennis at Slinfold Tennis Club
- Dodgeball with Academy Stars Coaching
- Footgolf at Rookwood Golf Course
- Netball with Mrs Harvey
- Zumba with Mrs Barter
In addition to this, we had Olympic Gymnast Danusia Francis join us on the final day!
Olympic Gymnast Danusia Francis Visits Slinfold!
Sports Day 2024
On Wednesday 26th June, we held our annual sports day at Slinfold Cricket Club. Even though it was extremely warm, the children competed in each event with enthusiasm and showed great sportsmanship to their fellow teammates! It was great to see so many parents, grandparents and extended families coming out to join us for this fantastic event.
On Wednesday 5th June, we took 12 children to the Horsham Locality Stoolball Tournament. As this is not a sport we often play, the children showed great resilience and determination during each game and scored many runs. They showed great enthusiasm and worked incredibly well as a team. Another great sporting success!
On Tuesday 21st May, 12 children went to Billingshurst swimming pool for a locality swimming gala. 4 children took part in individual races and 8 took part in relays. All the children swam incredibly well, with some winning their races. As a team, Slinfold came 3rd! What an amazing achievement. Well done Team Slinfold!
Our football team at Slinfold welcomed Shelley School for a local fixture as part of the Horsham Schools Football League. The match was hotly contested from beginning to end with some great interplay from both teams. The match ended 4 – 2 with goals from George (2), Mason (1) and Fynn (1). The team was captained by Theo, who showed great resilience after a hefty tackle to lead his team on to victory. Archie was a strength in defence and used a cool head to clear many probing runs from the opposition. A great game and every player should be hugely proud of themselves!
Our super swimmers had a great time at the swimming gala. They all gave their best and had a wonderful experience. The competition was tough, and it was great to see the resilience and courage of our team. A great well done!
On Tuesday 26th March, a group of our Year 5 and 6 children attended Horsham Rugby Club to take part in a tag rugby tournament. They had an opportunity to play against other locality schools and showed great resilience and perseverance during what were some very tough games.
On Tuesday 12th March, a group of our Year 3 and 4 children attended a tennis festival. They had an opportunity to practise their tennis skills and play matches against other competitors. The children thoroughly enjoyed this opportunity and showed great sportsmanship throughout the festival.
Southwater vs Slinfold 6th March 2024
With the 1st half underway, Southwater had kicked off and managed to slip past the defenders and beat the keeper with a shot to the left to make it 1–0. The stern Slinfold defence held on for the second half, weathering shot after shot. In the second half, Slinfold sadly made mistake after mistake, resulting in another score for Southwater. Determined, Slinfold fought back, making the score 2-1. Southwater’s attack came again from the left winger. The keeper managed the initial save, but the rebound from the post was tapped in, making it 3-1. Southwater then went into 6th gear and goal after goal went by. There was not much hope for Slinfold, but they went again and managed to score one more before the end. The final score was 7-2. A huge well done to both teams and especially well done to Slinfold for showing courage and resilience.
On Wednesday 17th January, 11 of the Year 6 children went to The Weald School for a Tag Rugby tournament. We started off the session with some drills, and then we got to play some matches. They were really fun, and we improved our skills throughout. Although we were covered in mud, it was so worth it, we had such a great time!
Netball fixture against Pennthorpe School
On Monday 15th January, some of our Year 6 netball team took part in a netball match against Pennthorpe School. In the first quarter, the team showed great sportsmanship, and we won 5–0. Our lucky strike continued into the second quarter where we gained a further 5 goals, ending the match with a 10-0 win for us.
For the second half of the game, we mixed the teams up, which gave us all a chance to play with some other team members. It was a really fun match, and we look forward to returning to play them again.
Written by Lily and Jasmine
On Monday 22nd January, we hosted a football match against Greenway, as part of the Horsham School's Football league. The team played an incredible match, and we were leading in the first half 4-2. The second half proved a harder match, with the game ending in an 8–4 defeat. The team all showed incredible resilience, perseverance and our school values of respect, compassion, courage and responsibility.
Horsham Schools Football League
On Friday 24th November, Slinfold hosted Nuthurst for their second match of the Horsham School's Football league. The game was a tough match, with George and Carter scoring some brilliant goals. The games ended in a 5–3 win for Slinfold.
Girls Tag Rugby
On Thursday 23rd November, 10 of our Year 5 and 6 children attended a Girls Tag Rugby event held at Millais School. The girls played 3 games, 2 of which they won. All the girls showed great sportsmanship and displayed our school values throughout.
KS1 Multi Skills
On Wednesday 22nd November, the Year 2 children had the chance to visit The Weald for a Multi-Skills event. They took part in different activities to help develop their agility, ball control and team work. They all had a brilliant time and enjoyed the opportunity to try new things. The children showed courage to try something new and compassion by helping their friends when they found something tricky.
Weald Locality Cross Country
On Wednesday 8th November, 27 of our Year 3, 4, 5 and 6 children went to The Weald Cross Country event. All the children ran amazingly well, considering how wet the field was! The team results were as followed:

On Monday 6th November, our Year 5 and 6 Football team attended Leechpool Primary to play their first match in the Horsham Schools Football League. The team played incredibly well and showed fantastic team work and sportsmanship throughout the game. Having taken an early lead, with Carter scoring the first goal, the game ended in a 4–1 defeat.
2022 - 2023 - Sports Reports
On Wednesday 24th May, our Year 3 and 4 and our Year 5 and 6 football teams each played a friendly match against Arunside School. Both games were played with enthusiasm, enjoyment and in the true values of the school. There were plenty of goals too! Well done to all involved, a special thanks to Mr Evershed for organising and Mr Rangecroft for refereeing.
On Monday 12th June, 4 children attended the Year 5 Dance Workshop at The Weald Secondary School. The 4 children had a fantastic time learning different dances and composing their own pieces of dance. They all performed with confidence and enthusiasm. Well done girls!
KS1 Multi Skills
On Wednesday 26th April, some of our KS1 children took part in a Multi-Skills event at The Weald School. The children completed a range of sporting activities throughout the afternoon and displayed impeccable behaviour. Working well as a team, all the children showed our school values of Courage, Compassion, Respect and Responsibility. Well done Year 1!
KS2 Football Friendly
A fantastic time was had by all at our football friendly with Arunside. All the children represented the school brilliantly and worked extremely well as a team. Slinfold won our first match 7-1 with goals being scored by Carter, Mason, Ewan and Fynn. The second match was won by Arunside 5-3 with goals being scored by Carter and Tate. A wonderful time was had by all despite the rainy weather!
On 3rd March, some of our Year 3 and 4 children attended Horsham Rugby Club for a Tag Rugby Festival. Despite the cold weather, it did not dampen the children's spirits. The children played extremely well in all of their matches with some children winning over 15 belts. All the children showed determination, perseverance and great team spirit! Well done!
Cross Country Run
On Tuesday 21st February, 12 children attended the Horsham Schools Cross Country Run held at Christ Hospital. All the runners showed great determination and courage throughout the course and supported each other over the finish line.

Wrap around care
We are very pleased to be able to offer our community wrap-around care provision through 'The Hub'.
The Hub runs Monday to Thursday.
In the morning, the children can arrive from 7:30 for breakfast club. We then drop the children at their classes for 8:35.
After school, The Hub runs from 15:10 to 18:00. Children are provided with a range of different activities in a safe and nurturing environment. A hot meal is provided for dinner.
For more information and to book your child's place, please contact the school office on: 01403 790253.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Intent
At Slinfold Church of England Primary school we provide an enquiry based curriculum where discovery, questioning and discussion underpins the knowledge and skills we want our children to develop. Teachers are aware of the end points of the curriculum content and work backwards from these using road maps and opportunities for the children to discover and question key concepts of interest relating to the topic. Teachers and staff act as facilitators in enabling children to ask key higher order questions helping children to draw links between different subject areas.
Our learning cycles
We have 4 yearly cycle with 4 inter connected themes so that children are able to think about the bigger picture. These three themes of discovery, nature and reflecting on the past are vital in pupils being able to participate in the bigger situations they will encounter throughout the rest of their lives.
Reflecting on these big issues and helping children make sense of them will enable them to think about the bigger problems in life and how they will manage the social and emotional implications in a safe and secure environment.
We are firm believers in having fun through our learning. Many of the activities are designed so that children have a hands on, active learning approach to embed and develop key knowledge and skills. We use a wide range of different recording methods so that all children are able to feel successful in their education.
Writing within the cycles
Inclusive Practice
Our curriculum is constructed in a way that is ambitious and designed to give all learners, particularly the most disadvantaged and those with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), the substantive and disciplinary knowledge they need to succeed in life.
A knowledge focus is an inclusive approach. Knowledge is selected deliberately, focusing on the best of which has been thought and said in each subject, ensuring ‘cultural capital’ is developed for all. A knowledge focus has significant advantages for disadvantaged children as it ‘enables students to acquire knowledge that takes them beyond their own experiences.… Knowledge-led curricula attempt to provide young people with a school experience that enables them to be socially mobile, for this is at the core of what social justice is: enabling all people, regardless of socio-economic background, to be provided with the opportunities to succeed in life.’ (Young 2014).
Knowledge is embedded throughout our curriculum through retrieval practice, ensuring knowledge is remembered in the long term.
To find out more information about our curriculum please speak with your child's class teacher, speak with a member of the senior leadership team or follow this link to the national curriculum.
Quality First Teaching
All children attending Slinfold CE Primary School will receive high quality teaching that is personalised to meet the needs of all children. Quality First Teaching is a style of teaching that emphasises high quality, inclusive teaching for all pupils in a class. It includes well sequenced lessons coupled with effective pedagogical choices, and robust assessment for learning which is used to inform the next steps in the teaching sequence for the children. Quality First Teaching places a strong focus on pupil participation in learning which sets high and realistic challenges.

As part of our Quality First Teaching approach, we have a five-tiered model which provides a framework for teachers in order to make their teaching more accessible and inclusive whilst reducing underachievement.

School Clubs
At the beginning of each term, letters go out to parents inviting children to register for the extracurricular clubs on offer. These tend to vary from term to term. These usually take place after school, although some may be during the lunch break. Some clubs are run by school staff, others by outside agencies. (There is usually a charge for the latter.) We offer a range of sporting, creative and musical clubs each term.
This terms clubs include -
- Tennis (chargeable)
- Football (chargeable)
- Arts and Creative (chargeable)
